clue.text: Wretched hen parties are so topless

indicators.note: topless says the opening letter of the word is lopped off, its head removed

parts.note: a hen party is a women-only celebration before a wedding, so it has no men in it: it is chapless

explanation.surface: A grumble that bachelorette parties have become rather too risque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' looks like part of a racy picture, but it removes the C from CHAPLESS, the jokey word for a party without men.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone pitiably unfortunate, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Word of proclamation full of flavour, impressing sweetheart

indicators.note: impressing means pressing one thing into another, so a letter is set inside the word

parts.note: food full of flavour from herbs can be called herby
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A town crier's tasty pronouncement made with a lover pressed close.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal proclamations use this word to mean 'by this document or statement', so it is a word typical of them.

clue.text: If poet has long to compose, haiku heard here?

indicators.note: to compose means to put together in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet who longs to write a short Japanese poem might find inspiration in a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haiku' said aloud is 'hi, coo', the greeting of a bird; such cooing is heard in a pigeons' roost, so the definition is a playful one.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost for homing birds is full of cooing, which is what a 'hi coo' sounds like.

clue.text: An interest in action delights

indicators.note: in action means set moving, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that grabs your interest when it is happening live is a pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight people and to amuse them are synonyms, both meaning give them enjoyment.

clue.text: Flood: did the butterfly start to panic?

parts.note: the butterfly is a swimming stroke, so doing it means one swam

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Asking whether an insect fluttered off in fright when water rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butterfly' wants to be the insect; it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood something and to inundate it are synonyms, overwhelming it with water.

clue.text: Slippery slope dumping king and one knave in reservoir

indicators.note: dumping, with in, means dropping some letters down into another word
in shows where the dumped letters go, within the word for reservoir

parts.note: a sump is a pit or reservoir collecting liquid
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards
the Roman numeral for one is I
J is the jack, or knave, in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Playing cards being thrown into a pond on a slick hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A snow ramp for skiers to leap from is literally a slippery slope.

clue.text: Large stomach booted?

definitions.meaning: a roll of fat around a person's waist is jokingly called this
the extra wheel a car carries is kept in the boot, a British word for car trunk

explanation.walkthrough: 'booted' looks like 'kicked out'; it means 'stowed in the car's boot', the British term for the trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of belly fat is jokingly named after the reserve wheel kept in a car.

clue.text: Scaredy-cat's admission to the country

definitions.meaning: a coward owning up would say they fled
a nation of the Middle East

explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern state formerly called Persia is a country.

clue.text: Strip, as relative pinches hot bust

indicators.note: pinches means grips something between, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A family member steals a broken heater while undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a police raid in the surface but signals a scramble, giving OTH; 'pinches' looks like theft but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone and to undress them are synonyms.

clue.text: Pee on the throne with child

parts.note: the letter P is spelt pee
regnant means reigning, as a monarch on the throne

explanation.surface: A crude picture of a toddler on the potty with a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' looks like slang for a toilet beside 'Pee', but it is a monarch's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with child is an old phrase for expecting a baby.

clue.text: See 12
A piece of material hanging, height included a worrying drop

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so one letter sits within the word

parts.note: a valance is a short drape hanging around a bed or window

explanation.surface: A curtain with a measurement noted, looking at an alarming fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow crashing down a mountain is a frightening drop.

clue.text: A life's work for him

parts.note: read as one who devotes his work to writing an account of another person's life

explanation.definitionFit: Writers of life stories produce one person's life as their work.

clue.text: Total blue, Conservative

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling down
the political right is the conservative wing

explanation.surface: A Tory feeling utterly depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' also suggests the Tory party colour, but here it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Total and complete are synonyms here, as in an outright or utter disaster.

clue.text: Write about each thing involving love being very powerful

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so a letter is set inside
write about suggests rewriting, setting the letters down in a different arrangement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, looking like the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice to write about every object to do with romance, which is very intense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write about' turns EACHTHING into HIGHCTANE, and 'involving' puts O within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuel with a high octane rating is strong, so the phrase means potent.

clue.text: Pyramus and Thisbe, perhaps, "As You (Romeo and Juliet) Like It"?

definitions.meaning: the mechanicals perform this story inside A Midsummer Night's Dream
one Shakespeare title placed inside another

explanation.walkthrough: The brackets put one drama's name inside another's title, picturing a drama nested in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The story of Pyramus and Thisbe is staged by characters inside A Midsummer Night's Dream, an inner drama.

clue.text: Slow to allow attack, borders gone, I see

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: borders gone means the outer letters of the word are removed

parts.note: a charge is an attack
the letter C sounds like the word see

explanation.surface: Being reluctant to permit an assault, a commander has lost its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic people are sluggish, so slow is a synonym.

clue.text: Do the English, Welsh and Irish get off so?

definitions.text: Do the English, Welsh and Irish get off so?

parts.words: Do the English, Welsh and Irish get off so?
parts.note: the British peoples other than one group are free of that group, the Scots

explanation.definitionFit: Getting off unpunished is idiomatically escaping without penalty, here read literally as free of Scotsmen.

clue.text: Plan trap wearing mask, hiding face

indicators.note: wearing means having something around oneself, so the trap sits inside
hiding face means the first letter is covered and lost

parts.note: a veneer is a thin surface layer that masks what is beneath
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Someone sets a snare while in disguise, keeping their face concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin trap is a spring-loaded snare; 'hiding face' leaves ENEER, and 'wearing' is the container signal, as a face wears a mask.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome is to plan or contrive it.

clue.text: A third name ejected from drinking hole after having caught four of these in the mouth?

definitions.text: four of these in the mouth?

indicators.note: after having means the A piece follows the next piece mentioned, the letter for caught

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: third singles out the third N of the bar's name as the one to go
ejected from means thrown out of the word

parts.note: the nineteenth hole is golfing slang for the clubhouse bar

explanation.surface: A drinker is thrown out of the bar after being caught with a mouthful.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'nineteenth hole' is golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar after an 18-hole round; 'after having' puts the cricket C for caught first.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult humans have four pointed teeth named after dogs, so these are four in the mouth.

clue.text: Fate under the sea, some say, in the drink

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the fate word below the sea word

parts.note: French speakers say mer for the sea
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Someone's destiny lies at the bottom of the ocean, in the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the drink' sounds like 'in the sea', but the drink is the definition: a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine grape and its wine are an example of a drink.

clue.text: Item in wax, premier in candle material

indicators.note: premier in means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: rayon is a synthetic fabric or material

explanation.surface: Something embedded in wax, the top-quality stuff in a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax colouring stick for drawing is an object made of wax.

clue.text: Suddenly get something sticky?

definitions.meaning: to understand in a flash, informal British usage
a small stick off a branch, playfully called sticky

explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something suddenly is to cotton on, and a small piece of branch is a stick.

clue.text: Church built by racecourse

indicators.note: built means constructed from parts, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A church has been constructed beside a track for horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sacre-Coeur is the famous basilica on Montmartre in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris basilica of the Sacred Heart is a church.

clue.text: Approach rugby joke the wrong way

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke

explanation.surface: A gag about rugby told backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-up is the approach a bowler or jumper takes before the action.

clue.text: See 2
Instrument went backwards, snatched by evil sister

indicators.note: snatched by means taken inside the following word

parts.note: Regan is one of the wicked sisters in King Lear

indicators.note: backwards means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rode means went, travelled on a horse

explanation.surface: Someone retreated and was kidnapped by a wicked sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is one of Lear's two cruel daughters in Shakespeare's King Lear; 'backwards' gives EDOR, which she 'snatches'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium-style keyboard sounded by reeds is a musical instrument.

clue.text: See 14
Wayward boy squashing vermin

indicators.note: squashing means pressing something in, so a word sits inside

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
a rat is vermin

explanation.surface: A naughty lad flattening a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward and erratic are synonyms, both meaning unpredictable.

clue.text: English city ante-lithic? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ante means pre, and lithic means stone, so before stone is pre-stone

explanation.surface: Asking whether an English city predates the Stone Age.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire, northern England.
